paper.title_en: Probing cosmic anisotropy with galaxy clusters and supernovae
paper.abstract_en: Using $Λ$CDM and Padé-(2,1) cosmography, we study directional variations in the Hubble constant, $H_0$, using galaxy clusters (GC) and Type Ia Supernovae (SNe), from the PantheonPlus compilation, employing the hemisphere decomposition method. Since there is a degeneracy between $H_0$ and absolute magnitude $M_B$ for SNe, Cepheid-host calibration is usually required to constrain $H_0$. To complement the Cepheid-host calibration in the SNe analysis, we use GC X-ray scaling relations as a complementary probe of anisotropy. We consider five redshift bins on the full SNe sample $[z_\mathrm{min}, 0.5]$ where $z_\mathrm{min}= \{0.015, 0.03, 0.05, 0.1, 0.2\}$. Our results show that the combined GC sample is consistent with statistical isotropy and that there is a $\sim 2.5 σ$ anisotropy preference in the lowest-redshift bin in the SNe-only case. This preference weakens when low-redshift SNe are progressively removed. In the SNe$+$GC analysis, we find that any anisotropy preference is driven by how the $H_0-M_B$ and the $H_0-k$ (where $k$ is the normalization parameter in the GC scaling relation) degeneracies are treated. The low-redshift bin anisotropy preference in the SNe-only analysis persists in the SNe$+$GC case when Cepheid-host calibration is used while the results are consistent with statistical isotropy when $k$ is fixed. Overall, our results do not provide compelling evidence for a statistically significant anisotropy in the local expansion rate. Our findings highlight the importance of combining complementary cosmological probes and examining the dependence of anisotropy constraints on calibrations and parameter degeneracies when assessing claims of cosmic anisotropy.
